QUOTE: "The high-level part is `ret & 0xFF80`. It goes to `mbedtls_high_level_strerr()`... The low-level part is `ret & ~0xFF80`. If non-zero, it is appended after `\" : \"` with `mbedtls_low_level_strerr()`"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains the code splits into high-level and low-level parts and that the decoder renders both joined with " : " when both are present (e.g. "X509 - ... : ASN1 - ...").
